content.text:
Here's the side-by-side comparison, built from the code of both projects: our repo, and opencode at commit `b471c2b`.

### Trigger

| | Elemental Harness (`compaction-basic`) | opencode (`session/compaction.ts`) |
|---|---|---|
| Automatic trigger | Token usage ≥ **80%** of context window (`thresholdRatio 0.8`) | Tokens used ≥ **usable limit** = input limit − min(20k, max output), i.e. nearly full |
| Provider overflow error | Prunes, summarizes, retries (up to `maxOverflowRetries: 1`) | Compacts, then re-sends the interrupted user message; media replaced by placeholders |
| Manual | `/compact` | `/compact` |
| Turn off | `auto: false` | `compaction.auto: false` |
| Per-model settings | Yes (`modelPolicies`) | No; one global config |

### Stage 1: pruning tool outputs (no LLM)

| | Elemental Harness (`compaction-tool-result-pruner`) | opencode (`prune`) |
|---|---|---|
| Default | **On** in the web presets | **Off** (`prune: false`) |
| When it runs | Only when compaction triggers, before summarizing | After every completed agent loop, in the background, whether or not the context is full |
| Which outputs | **Every** tool result over 8,192 characters, including the latest | Only **older** outputs: skips the last 2 turns, protects the newest 40k tokens of output, never prunes `skill` |
| Minimum gain | None; any oversized result is cut | Acts only if ≥ **20k tokens** can be freed |
| What replaces it | First **4,096** chars + `[... tool result middle pruned ...]` + last **1,024** chars | The whole output becomes `[Old tool result content cleared]` |
| Original kept? | Yes, in the append-only log | Yes, in storage, flagged as cleared |
| Can the model get it back? | No | No |
| Can it avoid the LLM summary? | Yes: if usage drops below 80% after pruning, the summary is skipped (pressure trigger only) | No; the two are separate |

### Stage 2: choosing what to summarize

| | Elemental Harness | opencode |
|---|---|---|
| Kept word for word | Newest **16% of the context window** (`retainRatio 0.16`), or a fixed `retainTokens` | Newest **2k–15k tokens**: 25% of the usable limit, clamped |
| Cut point | Moved so a tool call is never separated from its result | Walks back over whole user turns, can split a turn; `tail_turns` can cap it |
| Summarized | Everything older than the kept part | Everything older than the kept part, minus earlier summary messages |

### Stage 3: the summary LLM call

| | Elemental Harness | opencode |
|---|---|---|
| Who summarizes | The conversation's own model by default; can be set to another (`summarizationProvider`/`Model`) | A hidden **"compaction" agent** with all tools denied; its own model if set, otherwise the conversation's |
| Format of the input | **Exact replay** of the last request: same system prompt, same tools, same messages | A **new plain-text transcript** (`[User]:`, `[Assistant]:`, `[Assistant reasoning]:`, `[Tool result]:` …) |
| Tool outputs in the input | As they are (already pruned to first 4k and last 1k if large) | Each **cut to its first 2,000 characters** + `[truncated]` |
| System prompt | The conversation's own | "You are a context summarization agent… Do not continue the conversation…" |
| Tools available | Tool list sent (for cache reuse); told not to call any | None |
| Provider cache reuse | **Yes**; only the final instruction is new input | **No**; the whole transcript is fresh input |
| Summary sections | Primary Request and Intent · Key Technical Concepts · Files and Code · Errors and Fixes · Pending Jobs · Current Work · Next Step · Critical Context | Objective · Important Details · Work State (Completed / Active / Blocked) · Next Move · Relevant Files |
| Key rules | Keep exact paths, commands, errors and IDs; quote user corrections faithfully; don't mention compaction | Keep exact paths, commands, errors, URLs and IDs; terse bullets; reply in the conversation's language; don't mention compaction |
| Earlier summary | One rule: merge rather than copy, drop outdated facts | Passed as `<prior-summary>` with **detailed merge rules** (newer wins, Active→Completed, anything not carried forward is lost) |
| Output limit | 8,192 tokens | Not set in the compaction code I read |
| Plugin hooks | Compaction is itself a replaceable plugin | `experimental.session.compacting` can add context or replace the prompt |

### Stage 4: checking the summary and swapping it in

| | Elemental Harness | opencode |
|---|---|---|
| Checks on the result | Rejects errors, truncation at the token limit, empty text and images; requires the summary to be **smaller** than what it replaces; retries once | Fails on overflow ("Session too large to compact"); I found no size check |
| Where the summary goes | One user message: an "automatic checkpoint, build on it" note + `<compacted-summary>` tags | An assistant message flagged `summary: true` |
| What the model sees next | Summary → kept tail → new messages | Compaction marker → summary → kept tail → new messages |
| Continuing afterwards | The note tells the model to continue without acknowledging the checkpoint | Adds a synthetic user message: "Continue if you have next steps, or stop and ask for clarification…" |
| Old history | Kept in the append-only log; replaying the session reproduces it exactly | Kept in storage; hidden from the model |
| Model can recall old history | No (proposed in the recallable-compaction note) | No |

### Summary

| | Better |
|---|---|
| How much detail reaches the summarizer | **Elemental**: full outputs vs 2,000-character cuts |
| Cost and speed of the summary call | **Elemental**: provider cache reuse |
| Kept tail on large-context models | **Elemental**: grows with the model; opencode caps at 15k |
| Headroom before overflow | **Elemental**: 80% vs nearly full |
| Choosing which outputs to prune | **opencode**: protects recent output; ours can cut the output the model is using |
| Merging an earlier summary | **opencode**: explicit rules |
| Keeping the summarizer on task | **opencode**: agent has no tools |
| Getting pruned or summarized content back | Neither |

The three improvements I suggested earlier target exactly the rows where opencode wins or both fall short: recency protection in the pruner, a spill path in the prune marker, and explicit rules for merging an earlier summary.
